object.title: Bounds for covariance and correlation of incident arcs in uniformly random DAGs
object.statement: Let $G=(V,A)$ be a directed acyclic graph, and consider two arcs incident on a common node. **Incident-arc range conjecture.** The covariance between the two arcs takes values in the interval $[0.08,0.140625]$ in modulus, while the correlation takes values in $[0.125,0.28125]$ in modulus. These ranges summarize values observed in complete enumerations for DAGs with three through seven nodes; their validity beyond the enumerated cases is not formally established.
object.source_name: Marco Scutari, “On the Prior and Posterior Distributions Used in Graphical Modelling”, arXiv:1201.4058 (2012).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.4058

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2012).

object.title: The $K_4^-$-density conjecture for $(K_4^-,C_5)$-free $3$-graphs
object.statement:
Let $K_4^-$ be the complete $3$-graph on four vertices with one edge removed, let $C_5$ be the forbidden $3$-graph, and let $\pi(K_4^-,C_5)$ denote the corresponding Turán density.

**The $K_4^-$-density conjecture.**

$$
\pi(K_4^-,C_5)=1/4.
$$

The lower bound comes from an iterated balanced blow-up of a $3$-edge, while the source gives an upper bound below $0.251073$; the conjectured equality is unresolved.
object.source_name: Victor Falgas-Ravry and Emil R. Vaughan, “Turán H-densities for 3-graphs”, arXiv:1201.4326 (2012).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.4326

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2012).

object.title: Conjecture on collecting all but one twelfth of a planar graph
object.statement: Let $G$ be a planar graph. To **delete** a vertex means to remove it and its incident edges. To **collect** a vertex means to remove it when its current degree is at most $4$; a set is collectable if its vertices can be collected in some sequence. **Collecting conjecture.** One can delete at most $1/12$ of the vertices of $G$ so that all remaining vertices can be collected. The collected vertices consequently induce a $4$-degenerate subgraph. The preceding results guarantee deletion of less than $1/9$ of the vertices, while the icosahedron shows that one deleted vertex may be necessary; the source presents the stronger $1/12$ bound as believed optimal and gives no resolution.
object.source_name: Robert Lukoťka, Ján Mazák and Xuding Zhu, “Maximum 4-degenerate subgraph of a planar graph”, arXiv:1305.6195 (2013).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.6195

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2013).

object.title: Armstrong's average-size conjecture for simultaneous core partitions
object.statement:
Let $s$ and $t$ be coprime positive integers. An $(s,t)$-core is a partition that is simultaneously an $s$-core and a $t$-core; its size is the sum of its parts. **Armstrong's conjecture.** The average size of an $(s,t)$-core is

$$
\frac{(s+t+1)(s-1)(t-1)}{24}.
$$

Equivalently, since there are $\frac{1}{s+t}\binom{s+t}{s}$ such cores, the sum of their sizes is

$$
\frac{(s+t+1)(s-1)(t-1)}{24(s+t)}\binom{s+t}{s}.
$$

The conjecture predicts a remarkably simple statistic for simultaneous core partitions and is the Catalan case of Armstrong's broader conjecture on simultaneous core partitions. The source presents it as a conjecture; no resolution is supplied here.
object.source_name: Richard P. Stanley and Fabrizio Zanello, “The Catalan case of Armstrong's conjecture on simultaneous core partitions”, arXiv:1312.4352 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.4352

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2013).

object.title: Fractional covering conjecture for separated d-intervals
object.statement:
Let $H$ be a hypergraph of separated $d$-intervals. Write $
u(H)$ for its matching number and $\tau^*(H)$ for its fractional covering number. **Fractional covering conjecture.** One should have

$$
\tau^*(H) \le d\nu(H).
$$
 This is known to fail for non-separated $2$-intervals, where an intersecting family can have $\tau^*\geq\tfrac{11}4$; whether every intersecting family of non-separated $2$-intervals satisfies $\tau^*<3$ remains open.
object.source_name: Ron Aharoni, Tomas Kaiser and Shira Zerbib, “Fractional covers and matchings in families of weighted d-intervals”, arXiv:1402.2064 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.2064

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2014). “An open question in is whether $\tau^*<3$ for intersecting families of (non-separated) 2-intervals.”

object.title: Wilf-equivalence of 2143 and 246135 with 2413
object.statement:
For a permutation pattern $\tau$, let $\tau$-avoidance mean avoidance of $\tau$, and for sets of patterns let $\beta
ot
i\text{ any pattern in }B$ be understood through the permutation class notation $\operatorname{Av}(B)$. Two pattern sets are **Wilf-equivalent** when their avoidance classes have the same enumeration. **The ${2143,246135}\sim2413$ conjecture.**

$$
\{2143,246135\}\sim 2413.
$$

This is an unbalanced Wilf-equivalence between a two-pattern set and a singleton pattern. The paper presents it as conjectural; a bijective proof preserving 3142-avoidance would also yield the corresponding equivalence with 3142 included.
object.source_name: Alexander Burstein and Jay Pantone, “Two Examples of Unbalanced Wilf-Equivalence”, arXiv:1402.3842 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.3842

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2014).

object.title: Blum's conjecture on tilings of hexagonal dungeons
object.statement:
Let $a$ and $b$ be positive integers with $b\geq 2a$. The **hexagonal dungeon** $HD_{a,2a,b}$ is the lattice region whose hexagonal contour has side lengths $a,2a,b,a,2a,b$ in clockwise order. A tiling is a covering of this region by tiles, each formed by two fundamental regions sharing an edge.

**Blum's conjecture.** The number of tilings of $HD_{a,2a,b}$ is

$$
13^{2a^2}14^{\left\lfloor\frac{a^2}{2}\right\rfloor}.
$$

This conjecture concerns an explicit enumeration formula for a family of perfect matchings, equivalently tilings, and was still open when the paper was written; the paper proves it.
object.source_name: Mihai Ciucu and Tri Lai, “Proof of Blum's conjecture on hexagonal dungeons”, arXiv:1402.7257 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.7257

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2014).

object.title: Armstrong–Hanusa–Jones average-size conjecture for core partitions
object.statement:
A partition is an **$(s,t)$-core** if it is simultaneously an $s$-core and a $t$-core, and it is **self-conjugate** if its Ferrers diagram is invariant under conjugation. For coprime positive integers $s$ and $t$, consider the finite sets of $(s,t)$-core partitions and self-conjugate $(s,t)$-core partitions, with size given by the number of cells in the Ferrers diagram.

**Armstrong–Hanusa–Jones conjecture.** The average size in each of these two sets is

$$
\frac{(s+t+1)(s-1)(t-1)}{24}.
$$

The conjecture concerns a common statistic on two related finite families of core partitions. The paper states that the self-conjugate case is proved using a bijection with lattice paths; the source therefore treats this conjecture as resolved.
object.source_name: William Y. C. Chen, Harry H. Y. Huang and Larry X. W. Wang, “Average Size of a Self-conjugate (s, t)-Core Partition”, arXiv:1405.2175 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.2175

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of May 2014); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

object.title: Shellability conjecture for $P_1$ intervals avoiding two patterns
object.statement:
Let $P_1$ be the permutation class denoted by $P_1$ in the source, and let $\pi$ be a permutation in $P_1$. Write $[\textbf{1},\pi]$ for the interval from the one-element permutation to $\pi$ in the permutation pattern poset. **Shellability conjecture.** If $\pi$ avoids both patterns $456123$ and $356124$, then

$$
[\textbf{1},\pi]
$$

is shellable. This is the positive formulation of the preceding obstruction claim; the source gives no evidence that it has been resolved.
object.source_name: Jason P. Smith, “Intervals of Permutations with a Fixed Number of Descents are Shellable”, arXiv:1405.2560 (2015).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.2560

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2014).

object.title: Armstrong's average-size conjecture for $(a,b)$-core partitions
object.statement:
Let $a$ and $b$ be positive integers, and let an **$(a,b)$-core partition** be a partition with no hook length divisible by either $a$ or $b$. For a partition $\lambda$, write $|\lambda|$ for its size. If $\gcd(a,b)=1$, then **Armstrong's conjecture.**

$$
\sum_{\lambda} |\lambda|=\frac{(a-1)(b-1)(a+b+1)}{24(a+b)}\binom{a+b}{a},
$$

where the sum is over all $(a,b)$-core partitions. Equivalently, the average size of an $(a,b)$-core partition is

$$
\frac{(a-1)(b-1)(a+b+1)}{24}.
$$

The conjecture predicts the total and average sizes of the finite set of $(a,b)$-core partitions; it was informally proposed by Armstrong in 2011 and later published. The supplied text does not state whether it has been proved or remains open.
object.source_name: Amol Aggarwal, “Armstrong's Conjecture for (k, mk + 1)-Core Partitions”, arXiv:1407.5134 (2015).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.5134

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2014).

object.title: Uniqueness conjecture for the 16-vertex triangulation of the real projective 4-space
object.statement: Let $\mathbb{R}P^4_{16}$ denote the constructed $16$-vertex triangulation of the real projective $4$-space $\mathbb{R}P^4$. **Uniqueness conjecture.** $\mathbb{R}P^4_{16}$ is the unique $16$-vertex triangulation of $\mathbb{R}P^4$. This would establish vertex-minimality and uniqueness for the triangulation constructed in the paper; the source presents the claim as a belief rather than a proved result.
object.source_name: Sonia Balagopalan, “On a vertex-minimal triangulation of RP^4”, arXiv:1409.6149 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.6149

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2014).

object.title: Dokos et al.'s major-index distribution conjecture for three length-four patterns
object.statement:
Let $\mathcal{S}_n$ be the set of permutations of $[n]$, and let $\mathcal{S}_n(\tau)$ denote the permutations avoiding the pattern $\tau$. For a permutation $\pi$, its major index is

$$
maj(\pi)=\sum_{i\in\mathcal{D}(\pi)},
$$

where $\mathcal{D}(\pi)=\{i\mid \pi_i>\pi_{i+1}\}$. **Dokos et al.'s conjecture.** The major index is equally distributed on the sets $\mathcal{S}_n(2413)$, $\mathcal{S}_n(1423)$, and $\mathcal{S}_n(2314)$. This is a refinement of Wilf-equivalence for permutation patterns; the source identifies it as a conjecture about patterns of length four or greater, without giving a resolution.
object.source_name: Huiyun Ge, Sherry H. F. Yan and Yaqiu Zhang, “On a refinement of Wilf-equivalence for permutations”, arXiv:1410.2933 (2014).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2014). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1305.6616](https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.6616).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.2933

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2014).

object.title: The worst-case value conjecture for unweighted trees in Tron
object.statement: Let an **unweighted instance** of \texttt{Tron} on a tree be an instance in which all vertex weights equal $1/n$, where $n$ is the number of vertices. The **unweighted-tree value conjecture.** Any unweighted instance of \texttt{Tron} on a tree has value at most $1/10$. The paper gives an unweighted tree with value $1/10$, and establishes the corresponding bound for weighted trees, but determining the worst-case instance for unweighted trees remains open.
object.source_name: Daniel Hoske, Jonathan Rollin, Torsten Ueckerdt and Stefan Walzer, “Playing weighted Tron on Trees”, arXiv:1412.4100 (2014).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.4100

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2014).

object.title: The differential multiplicity conjecture for nice exponents
object.statement: Let $L$ be a finite field of odd characteristic, and let $s$ be an exponent. Write $s\not\approx 1$ for the stated exponent equivalence relation, and call $s$ **nice** when it has the property defined in the source's preceding discussion. A differential multiplicity is the number of solutions associated with a differential of the power mapping. **The differential multiplicity conjecture for nice exponents.** If $s\not\approx 1$ and $s$ is nice, then $2$ is a differential multiplicity. The conjecture is based on numerical evidence for odd characteristics from $3$ through $31$; the supplied text does not state a resolution.
object.source_name: Daniel J. Katz and Philippe Langevin, “New Open Problems Related to Old Conjectures by Helleseth”, arXiv:1412.8530 (2015).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.8530

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2014). “This conjecture remains open for $p>3$.”

object.title: Extremal edge conjecture for unbalanced bipartite 1-planar graphs
object.statement:
Let $x$ and $y$ be integers with $x\geq 3$ and $y\geq 6x-12$, and let $G$ be a bipartite 1-planar graph whose partite sets have sizes $x$ and $y$. **Extremal edge conjecture.** The graph $G$ has at most

$$
2|V(G)|+4x-12
$$

edges.
This conjecture proposes the optimal upper bound in the sufficiently unbalanced regime, where the smaller part has size at most roughly one sixth of the larger part. The paper's preceding results provide matching constructions and bounds in this setting, but the stated optimality remains open.
object.source_name: Július Czap, Jakub Przybyło and Erika Škrabuľáková, “On an extremal problem in the class of 1-planar graphs”, arXiv:1501.00176 (2015).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.00176

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2015).

object.title: The Normal Graph Conjecture
object.statement: Let $G$ be a graph. A graph is **normal** if its vertex set has coverings by cliques and by independent sets such that every clique in the first covering intersects every independent set in the second. Let $C_k$ denote the cycle on $k$ vertices, and let $\overline{C_7}$ denote its complement. **The Normal Graph Conjecture.** If $G$ has no $C_5$, $C_7$ or $\overline{C_7}$ as an induced subgraph, then $G$ is normal. The conjecture was posed by De Simone and Körner in 1999; the source paper is titled “Disproving the normal graph conjecture,” so the claim is refuted.
object.source_name: Ararat Harutyunyan, Lucas Pastor and Stéphan Thomassé, “Disproving the normal graph conjecture”, arXiv:1508.05487 (2020).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2015). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1311.6561](https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.6561).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.05487

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of August 2015); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

object.title: Yakoubov's generating-function conjecture for 231-avoiding linear extensions of alpha-labeled combs
object.statement:
Let $K_{s,2}^\alpha$ be the alpha-labeled comb with spine parameter $s$ and tooth parameter $2$, and let $A_{231}(K_{s,2}^\alpha)$ denote the number of its linear extensions avoiding the pattern $231$. Let $C(x)$ be the generating function of the Catalan numbers, defined by

$$
C(x)=\dfrac{1-\sqrt{1-4x}}{2x}.
$$

**Yakoubov's conjecture.** The generating function of these numbers is

$$
\sum_{s\geq 0}A_{231}(K_{s,2}^\alpha)x^s=C(x\cdot C(x)).
$$

Yakoubov posed this as an open enumeration problem for alpha-labeled combs; the supplied text does not state a resolution of this generating-function conjecture.
object.source_name: Colin Defant, “Poset Pattern-Avoidance Problems Posed by Yakoubov”, arXiv:1608.03951 (2017).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.03951

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2016). “We now settle many of the open problems that Yakoubov proposed.”

object.title: McFarland's conjecture on reversible difference sets
object.statement: Let $D$ be a reversible difference set, meaning a difference set equivalent to its inverse under the relevant group operation. A Hadamard difference set is a difference set with parameters $(4u^2,2u^2\pm u,u^2\pm u)$. **McFarland's conjecture.** If $D$ is a reversible difference set, then either $D$ is a $(4000,775,150)$-difference set or $D$ is a Hadamard difference set. The source presents this as McFarland's conjecture after noting that McFarland constructed an abelian reversible $(4000,775,150)$-difference set; the supplied status is unknown, so its resolution is not established here.
object.source_name: Tomas Nilson and Peter J. Cameron, “Triple arrays from difference sets”, arXiv:1609.00152 (2016).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.00152

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of September 2016).

object.title: Generalized Shareshian–Wachs conjecture for proper circular arc digraphs
object.statement:
Let $\overrightarrow{G}$ be a proper circular arc digraph, meaning a digraph with no induced subdigraph isomorphic to either $\overrightarrow{K_{12}}$ or $\overrightarrow{K_{21}}$. Let

$$
X_{\overrightarrow{G}}({\bf x},t)=\sum_{j=0}^{m}a_j({\bf x})t^j
$$

be its chromatic quasisymmetric function, and call this palindromic polynomial **$e$-unimodal** when $a_{j+1}({\bf x})-a_j({\bf x})$ is $e$-positive for $0\leq j<\frac{m-1}{2}$. **Generalized Shareshian–Wachs conjecture.** The polynomial $X_{\overrightarrow{G}}({\bf x},t)$ is $e$-positive and $e$-unimodal. This generalizes the Shareshian–Wachs conjecture from unit interval digraphs to proper circular arc digraphs; the source does not specify its resolution status.
object.source_name: Brittney Ellzey, “Chromatic quasisymmetric functions of directed graphs”, arXiv:1612.04786 (2017).
object.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.04786

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2016).

object.title: Maximality conjecture for abstract birigidity matroids
object.statement:
Let $[m]\times[n]$ be a round set, and let an **$(m,n,a,b)$-abstract birigidity matroid** be a matroid on this set of rank $bm+an-ab$ in which every $A\times B$, with $A\subseteq[m]$ of size $a+1$ and $B\subseteq[n]$ of size $b+1$, is a circuit. Let $\mathsf{MR}(m,n,a,b)$ denote the correctability matroid of the tensor product of an $[m,m-a]$ MDS code and an $[n,n-b]$ MDS code.

**Maximality conjecture.**

$$
\mathsf{BR}(m,n,a,b)=\mathsf{MR}(m,n,a,b)
$$

is the maximal $(m,n,a,b)$-abstract birigidity matroid.

This conjecture is equivalent to an affirmative answer to an open question raised by Mason over 40 years ago concerning the most general possible tensor product of two uniform matroids.
object.source_name: Joshua Brakensiek, Yeyuan Chen, Manik Dhar and Zihan Zhang, “From Random to Explicit via Subspace Designs With Applications to Local Properties and Matroids”, arXiv:2510.13777 (2025).
object.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2014–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2404.07393](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.07393), [arXiv:1902.06262](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.06262), [arXiv:1408.2429](https://arxiv.org/abs/1408.2429).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.13777

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2025). “This conjecture is equivalent to an affirmative answer to an open question raised by Mason over 40 years ago on the most general possible tensor product of two uniform matroids.”
